title: Transport of one Proj twist along any chart comparison
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ carry its total-degree grading, let $P=\operatorname{Proj}S$ [def-nagata-affine-proj], and let $C:P\cong\mathbf P^1_k$ be a chart-compatible scheme isomorphism [def-sc-p1-proj-chart-isomorphism], with the standard chart convention of [def-sc-p1-standard]. For every integer $d$, the inverse pullback of the associated Proj twist [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] satisfies $(C^{-1})^*\operatorname{Proj.twist}(d)\cong\operatorname{ProjectiveSpace.twist}(d)$, where the latter is the inverse image of the integral-model twist [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. This assertion concerns one rank-one twist and assumes no auxiliary graded module, basis or supplied sheaf.

proof.text: On D(x_i) the degree-d part of the localized polynomial ring is free on x_i^d, for every integer d: multiplication by x_i^(-d) identifies it with the degree-zero part. The twist restriction is therefore free of rank one. On the overlap x_0^d=t^(-d)x_1^d. This follows from the local fraction definition of the twist and the standard chart ratio t=x_1/x_0.

The chart equations of C identify the transported generators with generators on the standard projective-line opens. The projective-space twist is pulled back from the integral Proj model. On each integral chart its trivialization is free on x_i^d; extension of scalars to k preserves that free module and maps the overlap coefficient (x_i/x_j)^d to the same ratio over k. Hence both transported and projective-space twists have the same two generators and transition relation, including negative d and d=0.

These rank-one chart data give TwistData on both modules. Apply the uniqueness of the glued twist to identify them: the local maps send generator to generator, agree on the overlap by the transition relation, and their similarly glued inverses give identity composites.

    (C : ProjectiveLine.ProjChartIsomorphism k) (d : ℤ) :

      (twist (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) d) ≅
